documents.subject: Liquidity
documents.author: Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing
documents.text: Call with the managing director of Oberflächentechnik Weißacher GmbH: he asked twice whether we could pay earlier and said the bank is watching every month. 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.'

documents.subject: Payment of invoices
documents.author: Oberflächentechnik Weißacher GmbH
documents.text: Could you pay our invoices within 10 days? In return we would grant a cash discount.

documents.subject: Overdue invoices
documents.author: Oberflächentechnik Weißacher GmbH
documents.text: Several of our invoices are overdue again. We ask you to keep to the agreed payment terms; otherwise we will have to review our conditions.

documents.subject: Holiday shutdown
documents.author: Oberflächentechnik Weißacher GmbH
documents.text: Our plant is closed from 23 December to 6 January. Please place call-offs for January by 10 December.

persona.summary: Founder-run coater (30 staff, EUR 2-5 M), sole source of our cover plate set. In financial distress: credit index jumped 248 to 343, rating downgraded, bank watching monthly, MD 'cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now'. Complains about overdue invoices. Quality is red and worsening (OTD 54 %, 5556 ppm, 3 open 8D). Open moderate: buy price with faster payment, use the scorecard, do not squeeze it into failure.
persona.notes: Needs cash: asked twice for earlier payment, quote remark requests 10-day payment. Fears the bank and late payers. Contradiction: says we pay late, yet we paid 6.7 days early on average taking 42 cash discounts; still 39 % of invoices over 5 days late. Contract already has 2 %/10 days. Sole source: supply risk if it fails.

avoid: hard margin squeeze on a distressed sole source
changing terms after its final offer
tactics: Open moderate and lead with guaranteed 10-day payment on all invoices: cash is what it needs.
Acknowledge the overdue invoices and commit to on-time payment as part of the package.
Use the red scorecard and 3 open 8D reports as the second argument.
Take a modest price step plus a quality improvement commitment; do not push it below a sustainable margin.
Accept its final offer if it is reasonable; walking risks supply of a sole-sourced part.
playbook.expected_concession: History: asked +1.9-2.8 % and settled 0 %; now resists any margin cut, so expect small moves bought mainly with faster payment.
